Visioner BIG | 🇺🇸 🇮🇷 ‼️ ‼️ Multiple US military aircraft are airborne over the Middle East tonight, raising questions about possible preparations for American strikes against Iran amid escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran. The aircraft currently operating in the region include four US Air Force KC-46A Pegasus aerial refueling tankers and one US Navy P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol and intelligence aircraft. The tankers can support extended combat air operations, while the P-8A provides maritime surveillance, reconnaissance, and intelligence capabilities. Their specific missions have not been disclosed. The combination of aerial refueling and maritime reconnaissance assets is consistent with the support requirements of a potential long-range strike operation against Iran. Tankers could extend the operational reach of American combat aircraft, while the P-8A could monitor Iranian naval activity and maritime threats. However, these deployments alone do not confirm that a US attack is imminent. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

Visioner BIG | 🇺🇦 🇷🇺 🇦🇱 🇱🇾 ‼️ ‼️ A naval attack drone that reportedly struck a Russian corvette off the coast of Libya is said to have launched from Albania, traveling more than 800 kilometers across the Mediterranean Sea before reaching its target. According to emerging reports, the unmanned surface vessel completed a long-distance maritime journey before attacking the Russian warship near Libya. The exact launch location, the drone’s operator, and the extent of damage inflicted on the corvette remain unverified. A successful attack over such a distance would demonstrate the growing reach of unmanned naval warfare far beyond traditional conflict zones. The reported launch from Albania would also raise significant questions about the operation’s logistical support and planning, while exposing potential vulnerabilities in Russian naval deployments across the Mediterranean. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

Visioner BIG | 🇷🇺 🇺🇦 🇱🇾 ‼️ ‼️ A Russian government Il-76TD transport aircraft has departed Benghazi, Libya, following reports of a Ukrainian naval drone attack against the Russian Navy’s Steregushchiy-class corvette Merkury off the Libyan coast. The aircraft, operating under flight identifier SUM9621 and belonging to Russia’s Ministry of Emergency Situations, arrived in Benghazi from Moscow earlier this morning before departing again. Its movements come shortly after the reported Ukrainian strike on the Russian warship. The aircraft’s cargo, passengers, and precise mission remain unknown, and no direct connection to the naval incident has been established. The timing of the flight raises questions about whether Moscow is mobilizing logistical or emergency support following the reported attack. A successful Ukrainian strike against a Russian corvette near Libya would demonstrate the expanding geographical reach of Ukraine’s maritime operations and expose vulnerabilities in Russian naval deployments far beyond the Black Sea. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

IDF fears unilateral attack on Iran could trigger multi-front war Israeli Military Intelligence has reportedly rejected Prime Minister Netanyahu and Mossad chief Gofman’s assessment that Israel could launch a ‘limited’ 3-5 day operation against Iran and get away with it without any repercussions. Instead, a new escalation could spark a regional war pulling in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, Israel’s Channel 12 reports, citing a closed-door security cabinet meeting at which the IDF’s intelligence service made its position clear to Netanyahu and top defense officials. Separately on Sunday, a source told Israel’s Kan broadcaster that Netanyahu continues to lobby President Trump to hit Iran “as soon as possible” despite reported reluctance on Trump’s part. Iranian officials, military and IRGC leaders have said they’re prepared for any escalation, and indicated that a resumption of full-scale fighting could mean Iranian attacks on previously not-targeted infrastructure like internet data cables and Big Tech interests, and may even expand the conflict beyond the borders of the Middle East. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
